solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Modern American elevated railway’s supporting pillar

blocks.note: the El is the US name for an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A remark on the pillars holding up a modern American overhead railway.
explanation.walkthrough: A newel is the post at the foot or turn of a staircase that the handrail rests on; the surface points at railway engineering instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central or end post supporting a staircase and its rail.

clue.text: Dickens hero heard metal buzzer?

indicators.note: 'heard' says the listener took in sounds, so the answer is spelt as the phrase is spoken.

blocks.note: nickel is a metal and a bee is a buzzer

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking what a Dickens hero once listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Nickleby is the title hero of Dickens's third novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Nickleby is the hero of the Dickens novel named after him.

clue.text: What will cut party organisers was arranged

definitions.note: 'What' stands for the plural things that will cut

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them in a new order, so the letters of 'was' are reordered.

blocks.note: whips keep a political party's MPs in line

explanation.surface: Someone asks what will trim a party once the organisers have arranged it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration, but the organisers are parliamentary whips, the officials who make MPs vote with their party.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipsaws are narrow framed saws, so they are things that will cut.

clue.text: Cordelia Lambert’s running for MP perhaps?

indicators.note: 'running' suggests things in motion, so the letters of the name move into a new order.

explanation.surface: News that a woman called Cordelia Lambert is standing for Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party; someone running to be an MP might well be one, which is why the definition carries 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat is one example of an MP, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: A speed measure with current prohibition involving one Mr Toad?

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so BAN wraps round the I.

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
Roman numeral one, taken inside BAN to make BIAN

explanation.surface: A description of Mr Toad's motoring: speed and a banning order.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is a speed-mad motorist, so the surface fits him; the question mark says he is only an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Kenneth Grahame's motoring toad belongs to the class of cold-blooded creatures that includes frogs and newts.

clue.text: Plant singly after November’s out

indicators.note: 'November's out' says the N has left, so it is removed from the word.

blocks.note: N in the phonetic alphabet, the letter removed from ALONE

explanation.surface: An instruction to plant things one at a time once November is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun definition; November is N in the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: aloe vera and its relatives are succulent species grown indoors and used in soothing skin gels.

clue.text: Be nosy about worker, male assistant and home help

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around, so PRY goes round ANT.

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy
the worker ant, taken inside PRY

explanation.surface: Advice to be curious about a worker, his male assistant and the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of four staff; in fact 'home help' is the definition and the rest builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry maid is a domestic servant working in the pantry, a kind of home help.

clue.text: Claims Indic tune in play could be this

definitions.text: Claims Indic tune in play could be this

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters could become something else, so they are rearranged.

explanation.surface: A tune claimed to be Indian, heard during a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: an Indian-sounding tune in a play would be incidental music, and the same letters rearrange to give it.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental music is music played during a stage play to set mood or cover scene changes.

clue.text: Island tropical nation exporting unknown reptile

indicators.note: exporting sends goods out of a country, so the unknown Y is sent out of the nation's name.

blocks.note: GUYANA without Y, an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A tropical island nation that ships out a strange reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exporting' means sending something out, so Y leaves Guyana; the surface reads it as trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard, so a reptile.

clue.text: Relative hack chasing writer up

indicators.note: one who chases comes behind, so HEW follows the other piece.
in a down clue 'up' means read from bottom to top, so PEN reads backwards.

blocks.note: PEN, a writer, read upwards in a down clue

explanation.surface: A relative who is a hack journalist pursues a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist next to 'writer', but it is the verb hew; 'chasing' puts it after the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain case by example: a brother's or sister's son counts as family, one kind of kin.

clue.text: Conservative member unhappy in retreat

blocks.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A gloomy Conservative party member sulking in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a party member next to 'Conservative', but it is a limb of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbdown is backing off from a stated position, the figurative sense of retreat used of politicians abandoning a policy.

clue.text: Pressure on friend to provide dope

indicators.note: in an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so P follows CHUM.

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure, placed on (after) CHUM

explanation.surface: Pushing a friend into supplying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs, but it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British insults for a foolish, gullible person; nothing to do with drugs here.

clue.text: Great splendour’s temptation ensnaring paragon of virtue

indicators.note: a snare traps something inside it, so LURE closes round ST.

explanation.surface: Grandeur's allure trapping even a virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' or 'has'. ST for saint is the usual shorthand for a model of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre means shine, and figuratively the glory or distinction that makes something impressive, as in adding lustre to an occasion.

clue.text: Good management being dear to the Beatles?

blocks.note: careful, thrifty handling of money and resources
the start of a song title from the Beatles' White Album

explanation.surface: Praise for sound management that the Beatles would have approved of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear to' reads as 'cherished by', but it completes the title of the Beatles song Dear Prudence, written about Mia Farrow's sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful, sensible management, especially of money.

clue.text: House in China with British kitchen appliance

explanation.surface: A house in China fitted with a British cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to look like the country, but it is the pottery. A hob is the British word for a cooktop.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a smooth glass-topped cooking surface heated from below is one sort of cooker fitted in British kitchens.

clue.text: Show less decorum chaps with tango confusion

blocks.note: to be wilder is to show less decorum

explanation.surface: Men dancing the tango badly and making a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: BE WILDER is read as two words, then MEN and T are added.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns describe the state of being puzzled and unable to make sense of things.

clue.text: What dry material is best for rebuilding wide roof

definitions.text: What dry material is best for

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the parts together again in a new form, so the letters are reordered.

explanation.surface: A builder asking which dry material suits a wide roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about roofing, but dry wood is best for burning: the answer completes 'dry material is best for firewood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewood is what dry timber is best used for, since damp wood burns badly.

clue.text: Deep-rooted — not out there, not lacking inmost character

indicators.note: 'lacking' means without, and the inmost character of NOT is its middle letter O, so that goes.

blocks.note: NOT with its middle letter O removed

explanation.surface: A description of something deeply rooted and not lacking a core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out there' is IN HERE, two words run together; the second 'not' is itself the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherent is built in and permanent, deep-rooted.

clue.text: Purification of water in foul Ionian deltas

indicators.note: 'foul' in its sense of fouled up or spoilt, so the letters are jumbled.

explanation.surface: Cleaning up the water in the dirty river deltas of the Ionian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' sits naturally beside dirty water, which disguises it as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Desalination removes salt from seawater to make it drinkable, a form of purification.

clue.text: Reveal work of mischievous children?

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: Showing off the artwork made by naughty kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is being split into two words and read whimsically as the art made by mischievous children.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to impart news or secrets is to make them known, disclose or tell them.

clue.text: A new record set over a country

indicators.note: to set something over is to turn it upside down, so LOG reads upwards.

explanation.surface: A new record set in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set over' looks like part of a sporting record, but it tells you to flip LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Angola is one nation among many, on Africa's south-west coast, formerly a Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Something plucked from within commando lines

indicators.note: 'from within' says the letters are taken from inside the words that follow.

explanation.surface: Someone pulled out from behind commando lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucked' reads as rescued from enemy lines, but a mandolin's strings are plucked.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the mandolin's paired strings are played with a plectrum, so it is one instrument whose strings get sounded that way.

clue.text: Unit previous to being led by a politician

indicators.note: to be led by something is to come behind it, so ERE follows A MP.

explanation.surface: A military unit that used to be commanded by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' suggests a team, but it is the unit of electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the ampere measures electric current, one of the seven SI base measurements.

clue.text: Worry about being repetitive

indicators.note: to be repetitive is to say the same thing twice, so 'about' is given two ways in a row.

blocks.note: re = about, concerning, as in memo headers; the same word said again

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about saying the same thing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as part of 'worry about', but it is wordplay used twice over: once as CA (circa) and once as RE (regarding).
explanation.definitionFit: Care is worry or anxiety, as in 'without a care'.

clue.text: Affair of the heart of course that’s a short time earlier

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the central letters of COURSE are taken.
'earlier' puts A MO before UR in the answer.

explanation.surface: A love affair that everyone saw coming a moment before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair of the heart' looks like the definition, but only 'Affair' is; 'the heart of course' is the middle of COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: Memorial goes to Newcastle area

blocks.note: Newcastle is in the North East of England

explanation.surface: A memorial being moved up to the Newcastle area.
explanation.walkthrough: HEADS TO runs straight into NE with the word break hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is a memorial stone at the head of a grave.

clue.text: Easy to manage fare on returning vehicle

indicators.note: in an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so TABLE follows the vehicle.
returning is going back, so CART reads backwards.

blocks.note: the table one keeps is the food one serves

explanation.surface: Food served on a vehicle on the way back is easy to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price next to 'vehicle', but it means food, as in 'keeps a good table'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tractable people or materials are docile, compliant and easily handled or shaped.

clue.text: Cranwell and Dartmouth establishments’ trainee, primarily?

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so the first letter of each word is taken.

explanation.surface: A trainee at the RAF and Royal Navy colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF Cranwell and Britannia Royal Naval College, Dartmouth are Britain's air force and naval officer academies, so the whole clue also describes a cadet.
explanation.definitionFit: Officer trainees at Cranwell and Dartmouth are called cadets.
